primitives.name: Style Formula Derivation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Interface in one paragraph:** the pipeline derives ONE text string (the STYLE FORMULA) per game, gets it user-approved once, then inserts it byte-identical into every asset-generation prompt of every subsystem (sprites, animations, tiles, backgrounds, textures, 3D).
primitives.assumptions: All asset generation is independent; style formula is fixed post-approval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S is not uniformly applied across subsystems, visual inconsistency emerges.

layer2.mapping: The style formula acts as a global isomorphism between subsystems, ensuring that each asset generation process respects a shared stylistic kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-subsystem visual coherence score, measured via perceptual hashing of generated assets.

primitives.verbatim_quote: - **The perspective word in block 5 must match the genre**: platformer / runner → `side-view`; top-down → `top-down`; puzzle / clicker → `flat frontal`.
primitives.assumptions: Genre determines perspective; mismatch leads to visual dissonance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P ≠ f(G), cross-asset perspective misalignment occurs.

layer2.mapping: Perspective word P is derived from genre G and embedded into the style formula kernel to enforce spatial consistency.
layer2.telemetry: Asset-level perspective tag consistency rate across subsystems.

The derivation of the formula is a structured composition of stylistic blocks, each contributing to a unified aesthetic grammar. The perspective word alignment enforces genre-specific spatial semantics, preventing cross-asset visual contradictions. The style token is a compressed representation of this structure, designed for efficient communication in constrained environments. Failure modes arise when the formula is not consistently applied or when the perspective word does not align with genre expectations, leading to visual fragmentation. The system’s robustness depends on the invariance of the style formula under all subsystems and its preservation during transmission.
